t:
(a) 
That subparagraphs (a) to (j), inclusive, of paragraph II, part I, Veterans Regulation Numbered 1 (a), as amended, are hereby amended to read as follows:


“(a) 
If and while the disability is rated 10 per centum the monthly compensation shall be $15.


“(b) 
If and while the disability is rated 20 per centum the monthly compensation shall be $30.


“(c) 
If and while the disability is rated 30 per centum the monthly compensation shall be $45.


“(d) 
If and while the disability is rated 40 per centum the monthly compensation shall be $60.


“(e) 
If and while the disability is rated 50 per centum the monthly compensation shall be $75.


“(f) 
If and while the disability is rated 60 per centum the monthly compensation shall be $90.


“(g) 
If and while the disability is rated 70 per centum the monthly compensation shall be $105.


“(h) 
If and while the disability is rated 80 per centum the monthly compensation shall be $120.


“(i) 
If and while the disability is rated 90 per centum the monthly compensation shall be $135.


“(j) 
If and while the disability is rated as total the monthly compensation shall be $150.”



 
    (b) 
Paragraph IV of part 1 of Veterans Regulation Numbered 1 (a), as amended, is hereby amended by striking out “widow with one child, $100 (with $15 for each additional child)” and inserting in lieu thereof “widow with one child, $105 (with $25 for each additional child)”.

fable.w: The section directly sets monthly disability compensation rates and a widow's rate by statutory amendment. The tempting reading is that the reference to a "Veterans Regulation" implies rulemaking, but here Congress itself rewrites the regulation's text and gives no agency any rulemaking authority. No comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, or right to sue appears anywhere in the section.

qwen_block.w: This section establishes the specific monetary amounts for veterans' disability compensation based on disability ratings. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or decision-making process with parties outside the federal government. The definition explicitly excludes applications for benefits or grants, and this text merely sets the benefit levels rather than creating a participatory mechanism.
qwen_block.s: If and while the disability is rated 10 per centum the monthly compensation shall be $15.

opus.w: The section sets new monthly disability compensation amounts and survivor benefit amounts by directly amending Veterans Regulation No. 1(a). It creates no comment period, hearing, advisory body, outside consultation, or right to sue. The word 'Regulation' could make it look like rulemaking, but the statute itself makes the change. No agency is given authority to issue regulations, and the benefits involved are not participation.
opus.b: This section is a "No." Someone might read it as a "Yes" because it amends a "Veterans Regulation." But the amendment is made directly by statute. It just resets benefit amounts. It doesn't give an agency any new power to make rules, and it doesn't involve anyone outside the federal government.

qwen_chat.w: This section defines the specific monetary amounts of compensation for veterans based on their disability ratings. It is a substantive provision regarding benefits, not a procedural requirement for public participation or consultation with outside entities. There is no mention of hearings, comments, advisory boards, or coordination with non-federal parties.
qwen_chat.s: If and while the disability is rated 10 per centum the monthly compensation shall be $15.
qwen_chat.b:
Temptation: Nothing. The text sets specific dollar amounts for compensation based on disability ratings.
Resolution: This is a straightforward definition of benefit amounts. It does not involve any consultation, public comment, or interaction with outside parties in the decision-making process.
